question: Why do you need to be extra careful with cleaning liquids on a smart bed?

options.A: Infection control policies do not apply to automated furniture
options.B: Standard hospital beds never require chemical disinfectants
options.C: Smart bed mattresses are made of disposable paper materials
options.D: Smart beds have electronic panels and crevices where liquid can damage components

explanation: Because of all the wires and electronic touchpads, you must clean carefully so liquid doesn't seep inside and break the bed.

question: How does extreme poverty in a crisis zone directly lead to more gender-based violence?

options.A: It forces community elders to banish all young people from the camp
options.B: It causes international agencies to close down all local hospitals
options.C: It eliminates the ability of health workers to diagnose physical injuries
options.D: It drives individuals into dangerous transactional relationships and survival sex

explanation: When people have zero money or food, opportunistic predators take advantage of that desperation by demanding sexual favors for basic survival items.

question: How deep should the blade go when performing a standard skin snip?

options.A: Superficially into the dermis without deep cutting
options.B: Strictly through the dead outer stratum corneum layer
options.C: Deep into the subcutaneous fat layer for fat cells
options.D: Through the entire muscle layer down to the bone

explanation: You got it! Since the little parasites hang out in the upper skin layers (dermis), we only need a very shallow snip.

question: Where should a nurse document an accidental medication mishap or patient fall?

options.A: Inside the personal diary of the ward manager
options.B: On the front cover of the patient's bed chart
options.C: In a public text message sent to local news stations
options.D: On a separate institutional incident report form

explanation: Incident reports are kept separate from the official medical record to track safety data and improve hospital systems. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h8)

question: After identifying that a client's primary caregiver is exhausted, what is the best holistic nursing action?

options.A: Connect the family with local respite care and social work services
options.B: Tell the family member to stop worrying and sleep at the hospital
options.C: Ignore the finding since it is a family personal matter
options.D: Discharge the client immediately so the caregiver can rest

explanation: Collaborating with social workers to arrange respite care directly addresses caregiver burnout and supports safe home recovery. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h8)

question: A patient with a history of FGM complains of severe lower abdominal pain every month during her menstrual period, but no blood passes. What condition does this describe?

options.A: Cryptomenorrhea due to outflow obstruction
options.B: Ectopic pregnancy in the abdominal cavity
options.C: Pelvic inflammatory disease from a viral infection
options.D: Normal hormonal fluctuation during ovulation

explanation: When scar tissue completely or nearly blocks the vaginal opening, menstrual blood cannot escape, leading to painful accumulation inside the vagina and uterus. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which of these everyday ward items belongs to the general waste category?

options.A: Food wrappers from the ward kitchen
options.B: Used hypodermic needles
options.C: Surgically removed tissue samples
options.D: Expired antibiotic tablets

explanation: That's correct! General waste is non-hazardous and similar to ordinary household rubbish, like paper and food packaging.

question: What critical instruction must a nurse give a patient before they apply a fresh transdermal patch?

options.A: Apply the new patch directly on top of the old patch
options.B: Wash the old patch with soap and leave it in place
options.C: Remove the old patch before putting on the new one
options.D: Cut the new patch in half to double the lifespan

explanation: Leaving an old patch on while applying a new one causes dangerous drug overdosing because medication continues to absorb from both patches. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h8)

question: Why are human reservoirs who show no symptoms harder to manage during an outbreak than sick patients?

options.A: They refuse to take any form of laboratory testing
options.B: Their immune systems are naturally immune to all treatments
options.C: The germs they carry are invisible to standard microscopes
options.D: They continue normal daily activities and spread germs unknowingly

explanation: Because healthy carriers do not feel sick, they do not isolate themselves, allowing them to pass pathogens to many people during routine interactions. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h2)

question: A patient with advanced, progressive cancer is admitted for rehab. Which goal makes the most sense?

options.A: Maximizing comfort and dignity
options.B: Reversing all chemotherapy side effects
options.C: Restoring pre-treatment athletic ability
options.D: Preventing future tumor growth

explanation: When the disease is advanced, our main priority shifts to keeping the patient comfortable, peaceful, and full of dignity.

question: How does holistic care differ from traditional medical care that only looks at the disease?

options.A: It focuses only on spiritual counseling during illness
options.B: It integrates physical treatments with emotional and social support
options.C: It completely replaces modern medicine with herbal remedies
options.D: It ignores laboratory results in favor of patient feelings

explanation: Great job! Holistic care doesn't throw out medicine; it simply combines standard medical treatments with a broad view of everything our patients need.

question: Which condition often brings a patient to a subacute care unit?

options.A: Active cardiac arrest requiring immediate chest compressions
options.B: Routine annual physical examination and blood tests
options.C: Undiagnosed chronic fatigue without any physical findings
options.D: Recovery following a total knee replacement surgery

explanation: Correct! Post-surgical recovery that needs intensive physical therapy is a classic reason for subacute admission.

question: Which neurotransmitter works to calm down electrical activity in the brain and balance things out?

options.A: GABA
options.B: Glutamate
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: GABA is the brain's main 'braking' system. It helps calm down nerve activity so things don't get too excited.

question: Why do cardiovascular complications develop in patients with long-term heart conditions?

options.A: Patients always stop taking their drugs entirely
options.B: Blood vessels suddenly become immune to pressure
options.C: Eating salt immediately cures heart disease
options.D: The heart's backup coping methods eventually fail under ongoing stress

explanation: Just like working out too hard without rest, the extra work the heart does to manage a disease eventually wears down its muscles and structure, leading to new problems.

question: What is a classic example of secondary prevention in a community clinic?

options.A: Building wheelchair ramps at public government buildings
options.B: Conducting physical therapy exercises for a patient who had a stroke
options.C: Teaching children how to use bicycle helmets to prevent head injuries
options.D: Screening adults for high blood pressure during a clinic visit

explanation: Secondary prevention means catching health issues early through screenings so we can manage them before they cause major damage.

question: What is the main goal of continuous bladder irrigation (CBI) after prostate surgery?

options.A: To deliver strong antibiotic drugs directly to the prostate tissue
options.B: To permanently shrink any remaining benign prostate cells
options.C: To measure the exact daily hormonal output of the testes
options.D: To prevent blood clot retention and keep the catheter open

explanation: After surgery, bleeding can form clots that block the catheter. CBI flushes fluid in and out continuously to keep everything clear and flowing!

question: What is the main goal of infection control when caring for patients right inside their own homes?

options.A: Eliminating all microorganisms from the domestic environment
options.B: Transforming the private home into a sterile hospital room
options.C: Reducing the cost of medical equipment maintenance
options.D: Breaking the chain of infection to protect clients and workers

explanation: Spot on! The big picture in home care is always stopping germs from spreading between you and your patient. You've got this!

question: Why do pharmacologists group sedatives and hypnotics together?

options.A: They both depress the central nervous system depending on the dose
options.B: They both have zero risk of physical dependence
options.C: They are both used exclusively in emergency psychiatric settings
options.D: They are both derived from the same plant extracts

explanation: Both drug groups slow down the central nervous system. Whether they just calm you down or put you right to sleep usually depends on how much of the drug is given.

question: A patient on a bedpan is struggling to urinate while lying flat. What should you try first?

options.A: Assist the patient into a more natural, upright sitting position
options.B: Restrict all fluid intake for the rest of the day
options.C: Insert an indwelling catheter immediately without further delay
options.D: Administer a strong diuretic medication by mouth

explanation: Gravity and a normal sitting posture help relax the muscles, making it much easier to pass urine naturally.

question: A community needs a ward-level facility that can handle 24-hour deliveries and minor procedures. Which one should they use?

options.A: Mobile immunization clinic
options.B: Traditional birth attendant post
options.C: Primary Health Centre
options.D: Health Post

explanation: The Primary Health Centre (PHC) serves as the bigger hub at the ward headquarters, fully equipped for round-the-clock deliveries and minor treatments.

question: Studying a rare medical condition, a researcher asks early patients to connect her with other patients they know. What technique is this?

options.A: Snowball sampling
options.B: Quota sampling
options.C: Stratified sampling
options.D: Systematic sampling

explanation: Spot on! Just like a snowball rolls and gets bigger, your participant list grows as each person refers you to the next.

question: Why are pure opioid agonists like morphine considered strong pain relievers?

options.A: They fully activate mu receptors to stop severe pain signals.
options.B: They never cause any unwanted side effects in the body.
options.C: They eliminate all inflammation directly at the injury site.
options.D: They only work on mild headaches and minor muscle sprains.

explanation: Morphine locks strongly onto mu receptors in the central nervous system, which is why it's so powerful at knocking out severe pain.

question: What is a crucial nursing responsibility during the recovery phase for a patient who survived severe asphyxia?

options.A: Stopping all vital sign measurements
options.B: Performing regular neurological checks
options.C: Encouraging heavy physical exercise right away
options.D: Restricting all family visits indefinitely

explanation: Keeping a close eye on brain function with regular neuro checks lets you catch any delayed complications early on. Great nursing care!

question: Why does severe anemia pose such a big risk to a woman during childbirth?

options.A: It leaves her with very little reserve to tolerate normal blood loss during delivery
options.B: It prevents the placenta from attaching securely to the uterine wall
options.C: It stops the uterus from producing amniotic fluid during the first trimester
options.D: It automatically causes the baby to develop severe congenital heart disease

explanation: Anemic mothers have low red blood cell counts, meaning even a small amount of blood loss during delivery can quickly lead to shock. This is why antenatal iron supplements are so crucial!

question: What is the main job of an antidote in poisoning cases?

options.A: A substance that neutralizes or counteracts a poison
options.B: A routine supplement given to boost immunity
options.C: A medication that cures all known drug overdoses
options.D: A chemical that completely destroys red blood cells

explanation: Think of an antidote as the specific counter-punch to a toxin. It is designed to bind to or neutralize harmful substances in the body. You've got this!

question: Why are patients receiving strong antibiotic therapy at higher risk for developing oral fungal infections?

options.A: Antibiotics kill normal protective bacteria, allowing fungi to overgrow.
options.B: Antibiotics harden the tooth enamel and trap food particles in the gums.
options.C: Antibiotics directly stimulate the taste buds to produce excess sugar.
options.D: Antibiotics immediately inflame the hard palate and block saliva ducts.

explanation: Broad-spectrum antibiotics wipe out the harmless resident bacteria that normally keep fungal populations in check within the oral cavity. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h7)

question: A state health board notices a sharp rise in infant mortality in a rural district through vital data. What action should they take first?

options.A: Increase taxes for citizens living in urban areas
options.B: Close all the primary schools in the affected region
options.C: Stop collecting birth data for the next five years
options.D: Direct more child health resources and immunisation teams to that district

explanation: When data highlights a specific problem area, health planners must channel targeted interventions directly to that community to save lives. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h7)

question: An asthma patient says they need to use their rescue inhaler every single day for wheezing. What does this tell you?

options.A: The patient is experiencing a normal, expected reaction to therapy
options.B: The spacer device is broken and needs to be replaced immediately
options.C: The patient is using the correct technique for daily maintenance
options.D: The underlying disease is poorly controlled and needs medical review

explanation: Needing a rescue inhaler more than twice a week is a red flag that the asthma isn't well-controlled, meaning the doctor needs to review their daily maintenance plan.

question: Why is it better to help an older patient sit in a chair for meals instead of keeping them flat in bed?

options.A: It saves the nursing staff time during meal distribution
options.B: It is a strict hospital rule with no clinical reasoning behind it
options.C: It completely cures chronic joint arthritis in the legs
options.D: It prevents muscle deconditioning and improves digestion and alertness

explanation: Well done! Sitting upright helps them swallow safely, digests food better, and keeps them awake and alert.

question: Which test gives the best quick check of oxygen, carbon dioxide, and acid-base balance in a crashing patient?

options.A: Full blood count
options.B: Urinalysis
options.C: Stool microscopy
options.D: Arterial blood gases

explanation: ABGs give you the full picture of how well the lungs are oxygenating the blood and clearing out waste gases. You'll master this in clinicals!

question: What is the main point of using motivational interviewing during nutrition counseling?

options.A: Testing the patient on their knowledge of food biochemistry
options.B: Allowing the nurse to firmly dictate strict rules for weight loss
options.C: Speeding up the clinical consultation to save hospital time
options.D: Helping patients resolve their ambivalence about changing eating habits

explanation: Spot on. Motivational interviewing helps patients work through their mixed feelings so they can find their own inner drive to change.

question: Which sign is most characteristic of emotional distress or depression in a neurologic client?

options.A: Asking too many questions about hospital food
options.B: Wanting to watch television all night long
options.C: A sudden increase in daily physical exercise
options.D: Loss of interest in hobbies and daily activities

explanation: Withdrawal and losing pleasure in things the client used to enjoy are classic signs of depression and low mood. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which prevention method helps protect vulnerable people in the community who cannot receive vaccines themselves?

options.A: Shutting down all municipal water treatment plants
options.B: Treating every citizen with broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Building community immunity through high vaccination rates
options.D: Isolating all healthcare workers in private quarters

explanation: When most of the community is vaccinated, it creates a shield of herd immunity that protects babies, the sick, and others who cannot take vaccines.

question: A hospital pharmacy keeps cash from drug sales in an open drawer and uses it to buy office snacks, leading to empty shelves. Which part of the DRF system is failing?

options.A: Quantification and forecasting
options.B: Manufacturing of raw chemicals
options.C: Revenue collection and banking
options.D: Patient disease diagnosis

explanation: Makes total sense, right? If cash isn't banked safely and gets spent on snacks, the revolving fund stops revolving, and drugs run out!

question: You hear gurgling sounds and see thick secretions in an unconscious patient's mouth. What is your very first action?

options.A: Turn the patient flat on their back and offer water
options.B: Administer a sleeping pill to calm the patient down
options.C: Wait for the doctor to arrive before doing anything
options.D: Suction the airway to clear out the secretions

explanation: Brilliant! Gurgling means the airway is blocked. Grab that suction machine right away to help them breathe easy again.

question: What is the biggest perk of doing a quick mental check-in with yourself at the end of a shift?

options.A: Eliminating the requirement for formal nursing handover reports
options.B: Ensuring that the morning shift arrives earlier than scheduled
options.C: Identifying workflow delays to improve future time management
options.D: Calculating the exact financial savings generated for the hospital

explanation: You're learning fast! Thinking about what slowed you down today helps you plan better and feel more confident tomorrow.

question: What is usually the very first step when putting together a new healthcare budget?

options.A: Borrowing large sums of money from local commercial banks
options.B: Reviewing past financial data and current patient trends
options.C: Firing staff to immediately reduce operational expenses
options.D: Purchasing expensive new diagnostic medical equipment

explanation: Before you can plan for tomorrow, you need to check yesterday. Looking at past records and patient numbers gives you a realistic starting point.

question: What is the main goal of doing a 'medication reconciliation' when a patient is admitted?

options.A: To compare home medications with new orders and prevent errors
options.B: To ensure the patient has enough food to take with their pills
options.C: To calculate the financial cost of the patient's prescriptions
options.D: To test how fast the patient's liver metabolizes oral tablets

explanation: Medication reconciliation is like doing a safety checkup on what the patient was taking at home versus what the doctor just prescribed, ensuring no dangerous overlaps slip through!

question: Why is blunt heart injury often harder to spot right away compared to a stab wound?

options.A: X-ray machines cannot take pictures of blunt force trauma.
options.B: The chest wall often shows no open wounds or obvious external damage.
options.C: The heart stops beating completely right away.
options.D: Symptoms only appear several weeks after the accident.

explanation: Because the skin and ribs stay intact, there's no open wound to warn you. That's why nurses have to stay alert for hidden internal bruising!

question: Which simple nursing action helps relax tummy muscles and ease pain for a patient having severe cramps (colic)?

options.A: Firmly massaging the lower abdomen in circles
options.B: Placing the patient flat on their stomach with a pillow
options.C: Encouraging them to take a brisk walk around the ward
options.D: Elevating the head of the bed and bending their knees

explanation: Bending the knees takes the tension right off the abdominal wall muscles, which instantly eases up the cramping pressure. Try it yourself!

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four legal elements needed to prove professional negligence?

options.A: Actual damages suffered by the patient
options.B: Direct causation of an injury
options.C: Guaranteed hospital bankruptcy
options.D: Breach of the legal duty of care

explanation: You got it! Hospital bankruptcy is just a financial state—it has nothing to do with the legal checklist needed to prove negligence in court.

question: What is the main goal of routine GI screenings like a colonoscopy?

options.A: To cure existing advanced infections instantly without medicine
options.B: To detect polyps and early-stage cancer before symptoms start
options.C: To measure the exact daily caloric intake of the patient
options.D: To replace the need for healthy eating and hydration

explanation: Screening lets doctors catch tiny growths or early changes long before they turn into major problems.

question: What happens during the process of clot retraction?

options.A: White blood cells destroy excess fibrinogen in the plasma
options.B: Platelets contract to pull the edges of the broken vessel together
options.C: The blood pressure drops to prevent further vessel damage
options.D: Red blood cells multiply to replace the lost fluid volume

explanation: Clot retraction tightens the meshwork and draws the wound edges closer, which makes tissue repair much easier. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h5)

question: A patient complains that the hallway is too bright and noisy to sleep at midnight. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Explain that hospital noise is normal and the patient will get used to it
options.B: Move the patient to a bed located directly at the nurse's station
options.C: Close the patient room door and dim the overhead lights
options.D: Call the doctor immediately to request a strong sleeping pill

explanation: Simple environmental tweaks like pulling the curtains, dimming lights, and shutting the door work wonders before reaching for medications.

question: What is the primary purpose of performing a skin biopsy in dermatology?

options.A: To obtain tissue samples for definitive microscopic diagnosis
options.B: To instantly kill bacteria inside a deep skin abscess
options.C: To remove unwanted benign moles for cosmetic reasons
options.D: To rehydrate severely dry and cracking skin layers

explanation: A biopsy removes a small piece of skin tissue so a pathologist can examine it under a microscope to confirm diseases like skin cancer or severe inflammation. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of the cheeks and lips during the process of eating?

options.A: They keep food positioned between the teeth for effective chewing.
options.B: They absorb water from the food bolus before it reaches the stomach.
options.C: They filter out harmful bacteria found naturally on raw foods.
options.D: They secrete digestive enzymes that immediately dissolve tough fibers.

explanation: The muscular walls of the lips and cheeks press inward to keep food in the correct spot while the teeth grind it down. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h2)

question: Experienced nurses are resigning in droves because they feel invisible and unsupported. What should management do first?

options.A: Stop holding staff meetings to prevent nurses from voicing complaints
options.B: Issue strict warning memos about the consequences of resigning early
options.C: Establish structured mentorship and recognition programs for clinical achievements
options.D: Reduce salaries across all departments to save money for recruitment ads

explanation: To stop nurses from leaving, you have to show them they matter! Recognizing their hard work and setting up supportive mentorship makes all the difference.

question: Which serious complication of a peptic ulcer causes a hard, board-like abdomen and severe pain?

options.A: Pyloric stenosis
options.B: Perforation
options.C: Pernicious anemia
options.D: Gastric reflux

explanation: Spot on! If an ulcer burns right through the stomach wall, stomach contents leak into the belly, causing a medical emergency with a very rigid, painful abdomen.

question: Why do we keep the head of the bed slightly elevated for a patient with increased intracranial pressure from encephalitis?

options.A: To make sure the patient can see people walking into the room
options.B: To make swallowing oral pills easier
options.C: To help blood drain smoothly from the head and lower the pressure
options.D: To stop spit from going down the wrong pipe

explanation: Raising the bed to about 30 degrees uses gravity to help blood flow down smoothly through the jugular veins, keeping pressure inside the skull under control.

question: What is the most common type of fainting experienced by otherwise healthy people?

options.A: Vasovagal syncope
options.B: Orthostatic hypotension
options.C: Neurological syncope
options.D: Cardiac syncope

explanation: Vasovagal syncope is triggered by everyday events like pain, stress, or standing too long and affects most people who faint. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h2)

question: During a blood transfusion, a patient suddenly gets back pain, chills, and fever. What is your very first action?

options.A: Call the hospital laboratory to double-check the patient's name
options.B: Stop the transfusion immediately and disconnect the tubing
options.C: Slow down the infusion rate and grab a warm cotton blanket
options.D: Administer a dose of oral paracetamol for the rising fever

explanation: Stop it right away! Cutting off the flow prevents any more incompatible blood from harming your patient during a reaction.

question: What is the underlying cause of Sheehan syndrome after severe childbirth bleeding?

options.A: Lack of blood supply causing pituitary gland tissue death
options.B: A severe kidney infection spreading from the uterus
options.C: Permanent nerve damage from regional anaesthesia
options.D: An autoimmune reaction attacking the thyroid gland

explanation: Extreme blood loss drops the body's blood pressure so low that the pituitary gland gets starved of oxygen and blood, leading to tissue death (necrosis) and hormone imbalances later.

question: What should you do right after pulling the needle out of a PPD injection site?

options.A: Pat the area gently with cotton without rubbing it
options.B: Massage the skin vigorously to help absorb the fluid
options.C: Apply a tight pressure bandage to stop any bleeding
options.D: Clean the skin again with a fresh alcohol swab

explanation: Hands off that bubble! Rubbing or massaging can push the fluid away or mess up the skin test results. Just a gentle dab if needed. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h4)

question: Why do we place a footrest or pillow at the bottom of a cardiac bed?

options.A: To prevent the patient from sliding downward while in a sitting position
options.B: To provide a stable surface for the patient to attach leg exercise bands
options.C: To improve blood circulation directly to the lower extremities
options.D: To stop the mattress from sagging in the middle of the frame

explanation: You nailed it! Because the bed is propped up high, gravity tries to pull the patient down. The footrest keeps them comfortably in place.

question: What is the difference between a 'use-by' date and a 'best-before' date?

options.A: Use-by is for canned goods, while best-before is for fresh meat
options.B: Use-by relates to safety, while best-before relates to quality
options.C: Use-by is set by the government, while best-before is optional
options.D: Use-by means the food is free, while best-before means it is costly

explanation: Spot on! 'Use-by' is about food safety (don't risk food poisoning), while 'best-before' is just about peak flavor and crunch.

question: How long should a patient typically hold their breath after inhaling a dose of medication from an inhaler?

options.A: Until they feel dizzy
options.B: No more than one second
options.C: Exactly one minute
options.D: About 10 seconds

explanation: Holding the breath for about 10 seconds allows the tiny medication particles time to settle deep into the lung tissue instead of being exhaled right away. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the ultimate, primary benefit of using healthcare simulation in nursing education?

options.A: Eliminating the need for written exams and classroom lectures
options.B: Making sure nursing students never have to go to a real hospital
options.C: Improving patient safety and reducing medical errors in hospitals
options.D: Reducing the cost of running nursing schools and hiring staff

explanation: Every simulation exercise is ultimately aimed at protecting real patients by ensuring nurses are well-trained and competent. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h6)

question: What happens during the acrosome reaction when a sperm reaches the outer layers of an egg?

options.A: Enzymes are released from the sperm head to digest a path through protective layers
options.B: The sperm tail falls off completely to anchor the head inside the follicle
options.C: The egg swallows the entire sperm tail without using any chemical help
options.D: Protective antibodies coat the sperm to prevent premature entry

explanation: Think of the acrosome as a tiny chemical drill at the tip of the sperm head, releasing special enzymes to clear a pathway through the egg's defenses.

question: Which assessment gives the best practical idea of an older adult's functional independence?

options.A: Checking only the laboratory values for liver and kidney function
options.B: Evaluating the patient's ability to perform activities of daily living
options.C: Measuring the exact circumference of the upper arm muscles
options.D: Reviewing the family medical tree for inherited genetic conditions

explanation: Spot on! Checking how well a patient handles activities of daily living (ADLs) tells you real-world details about how safely they can live on their own.

question: When a registered nurse delegates a task to a junior colleague, who remains ultimately accountable?

options.A: The hospital chief medical director
options.B: The registered nurse who delegated the task
options.C: The junior staff member who performed the task
options.D: The patient's family members

explanation: Delegating a task shares the physical work, but as the RN, you keep the overall accountability to ensure it was done safely.

question: What is the primary goal of teaching oncology patients about emergency warning signs?

options.A: To ensure they seek help quickly before symptoms become life-threatening
options.B: To prevent them from ever experiencing another tumor recurrence
options.C: To train them to manage medical emergencies at home without calling a doctor
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of hospital stays

explanation: Early reporting of red-flag symptoms allows healthcare teams to intervene swiftly before minor issues become full-blown emergencies. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h7)

question: What are vulval varicose veins?

options.A: Benign fluid-filled cysts inside the myometrium of the uterus
options.B: Infections of the Bartholin glands located near the vaginal opening
options.C: Inflammation of the urinary bladder lining caused by bacteria
options.D: Enlarged and dilated blood vessels on the external genitalia

explanation: Spotting swollen, twisted veins on the labia or external parts can look scary, but they are just like varicose veins on the legs—they are simply enlarged blood vessels. You've got this!

question: A patient with severe dehydration is expected to show which kidney response regulated by hormones?

options.A: Low levels of ADH leading to dilute, high-volume urine
options.B: Massive secretion of sodium and water into the distal tubule
options.C: High levels of ADH leading to concentrated, low-volume urine
options.D: Complete stoppage of all tubular reabsorption in the cortex

explanation: Dehydration stimulates the release of ADH, causing the kidneys to conserve water and produce small amounts of very concentrated urine. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h8)

question: By about how much should a patient with symptomatic HIV who is losing weight increase their daily calories?

options.A: Up to 30 percent more calories
options.B: About 5 percent more calories
options.C: Double the normal daily intake
options.D: No change from normal intake

explanation: That's right! When the body is fighting active symptoms and dropping weight, it needs about 30% more energy to recover and maintain strength.

question: What does the term 'pulse deficit' mean in clinical practice?

options.A: A temporary drop in heart rate during deep breathing exercises
options.B: The time it takes for an electrical impulse to cross the AV node
options.C: A difference between the apical pulse rate and the peripheral pulse rate
options.D: A total absence of any detectable pulse in the lower extremities

explanation: A pulse deficit happens when the heartbeats are too weak to send a strong wave all the way to the wrist. When this occurs, your listening count at the chest (apical) will be higher than what you feel at the wrist (radial).

question: Which government program became the main payer for long-term nursing home care after 1965?

options.A: Medicare
options.B: The Hill-Burton fund
options.C: Social Security
options.D: Medicaid

explanation: Medicaid was built to support low-income individuals, and over time it grew to become the primary financial backbone paying for long-term stays in nursing facilities.

question: Why is building a trusting nurse-patient relationship so important for holistic care?

options.A: It allows the nurse to give orders that the patient must follow without question
options.B: It ensures the patient will never complain about hospital food or bills
options.C: It helps patients feel safe enough to share deep fears and personal concerns
options.D: It replaces the need for doctors to visit the patient on the ward

explanation: You got it! Trust creates a safe space where patients feel comfortable revealing the emotional and social burdens that impact their healing.

question: In community health, what does 'self-reliance' actually mean?

options.A: Patients treating their own severe illnesses without nurses
options.B: Villages building their own roads and electricity networks
options.C: Hospitals refusing to accept government grants or donations
options.D: Communities maintaining health improvements after external projects end

explanation: Brilliant! Self-reliance means a community has learned enough and built enough capacity to keep their health programs running smoothly even after the NGO or government project packs up and leaves.

question: What is a key nursing strategy for helping patients prevent complications from chronic skin conditions?

options.A: Teaching the patient how to recognize early flare-ups and avoid known triggers
options.B: Stopping all topical medications as soon as the skin looks slightly better
options.C: Using harsh antiseptic scrubs every day to remove the outer skin layer
options.D: Encouraging the patient to isolate themselves from family and friends

explanation: You got it! Empowering patients to spot early warning signs and steer clear of their triggers stops small issues from blowing up into major infections.

question: How does adding a little glucose to oral rehydration solution help the body absorb water?

options.A: Glucose creates a thick barrier that stops water from leaving the body
options.B: Glucose binds with sodium to pull water across the gut wall together
options.C: Glucose makes the drink taste sweet so the child will drink more
options.D: Glucose feeds the good bacteria so they can repair the damaged bowel

explanation: It's like a team effort! Sodium and glucose hitch a ride together on the same transport protein. As glucose is absorbed, it pulls sodium and water right along with it into the bloodstream.

question: Why must nurse researchers pay close attention to ethics during explanatory studies?

options.A: Because ethics boards only approve studies written in foreign languages
options.B: Because testing new interventions or manipulating variables can potentially affect patient safety
options.C: Because hospital patients prefer answering long questionnaires over resting
options.D: Because research ethics only apply to doctors and never to nurses

explanation: You nailed it! Whenever we test new methods or change care routines, keeping our patients safe is always the top priority.

question: An IV infusion of 1000 mL normal saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using an electronic pump. What is the rate in mL/hr?

options.A: 125 mL/hr
options.B: 150 mL/hr
options.C: 100 mL/hr
options.D: 80 mL/hr

explanation: Divide the total volume (1000 mL) by the total hours (8 hours) to get 125 mL/hr. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T6#GNS125_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the main difference between illness and disease?

options.A: Illness is how the person feels and experiences their sickness, while disease is the medical pathology
options.B: Illness can only be diagnosed with lab tests, while disease is purely psychological
options.C: Disease is a subjective feeling, whereas illness is an objective medical label
options.D: There is no practical difference between the two terms in nursing

explanation: Illness is subjective and personal, while disease is the clinical pathology diagnosed by a doctor. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is widely considered the gold standard of psychological treatment for ICT addiction?

options.A: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy
options.B: Strict physical punishment
options.C: Electroconvulsive therapy
options.D: Total isolation from society

explanation: CBT (the approach behind this app!) helps patients spot unhelpful thought patterns and build practical coping skills to manage their screen habits.

question: Why do nurses advise wearing cotton underwear when dealing with a yeast infection?

options.A: Cotton underwear prevents systemic absorption of the prescribed oral tablets
options.B: Cotton allows air circulation and keeps the area dry, which discourages yeast growth
options.C: Cotton fibers directly release natural antifungal chemicals onto the skin
options.D: Synthetic fabrics chemically bind to antifungal creams and block their action

explanation: Yeast loves warm, dark, and moist places. Breathable cotton keeps things cool and dry, making it a hostile home for yeast!

question: What hormone causes the rise in basal body temperature after ovulation?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Progesterone is a thermogenic hormone released after ovulation that slightly increases the basal body temperature. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T010#GNS226_U6_T010_h2)

question: Why do we often view rural villagers and urban slum residents as vulnerable populations?

options.A: They possess unlimited financial resources for private clinics
options.B: They always reject traditional and modern medical treatments equally
options.C: They have complete immunity against all infectious diseases
options.D: They face severe barriers to accessing affordable and quality healthcare services

explanation: Spot on! Distance, poverty, and a lack of nearby clinics make it really tough for these groups to get the standard care they deserve.

question: Which finding around a skeletal traction pin site means you need to call the doctor right away?

options.A: A small amount of clear dried crust around the metal entry point
options.B: The metal pin is visibly loose or wobbling
options.C: Mild skin redness close to the pin
options.D: Clear fluid drainage during the first day

explanation: You're doing great! Pins need to stay rock-solid in the bone. A loose pin messes up the whole traction setup and always needs a doctor's attention.

question: What does it usually mean if a patient's deep tendon reflex is very weak or missing entirely?

options.A: Hyperactive function of the spinal cord
options.B: Severe brain injury in the cerebral cortex
options.C: Excessive physical activity of the limb
options.D: Lower motor neuron or peripheral nerve damage

explanation: When a reflex pathway in the limbs is damaged or blocked, the physical response becomes sluggish or disappears.

question: Why is long-term intravenous therapy often administered via a PICC line for osteomyelitis patients?

options.A: It forces the antibiotic medication to bypass the stomach and land directly inside the infected bone cavity
options.B: It allows safe, long-term delivery of strong antibiotics directly into the bloodstream without frequent needle sticks
options.C: It prevents the patient from experiencing any side effects from the medication
options.D: It increases the white blood cell count within minutes of insertion

explanation: A PICC line provides reliable venous access for weeks of home or outpatient IV antibiotic therapy, sparing peripheral veins from damage. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of untreated or severe endometritis?

options.A: Normal spontaneous resolution without any treatment
options.B: Spread of infection into the bloodstream
options.C: Scarring of the inner uterine cavity
options.D: Formation of pus pockets in the pelvis

explanation: Endometritis is serious and won't just go away on its own. Leaving it untreated can lead to nasty complications like abscesses or blood infections.

question: Which of the following is a classic condition commonly managed using primary health care standing orders?

options.A: Neurosurgical trauma
options.B: Uncomplicated malaria
options.C: Open-heart surgery
options.D: Advanced chemotherapy

explanation: Uncomplicated malaria is a high-volume, routine primary care condition managed safely using standard diagnostic and treatment protocols. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h5)

question: What do we call pain or a burning feeling when passing urine?

options.A: Retention
options.B: Dysuria
options.C: Incontinence
options.D: Hematuria

explanation: Dysuria is just the medical word for painful or burning urination. Great term to keep in your clinical vocabulary bag!

question: Which legal document allows a patient to appoint a trusted person to make medical decisions on their behalf if they become incapacitated?

options.A: An insurance premium waiver
options.B: A durable power of attorney for healthcare
options.C: A standard last will and testament
options.D: A hospital discharge summary

explanation: This specific legal document designates a healthcare proxy or surrogate decision-maker to speak and decide for the patient when they cannot. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h6)

question: A patient keeps getting severe bacterial infections. Which lab values should the nurse check first to see how their antibody defenses are doing?

options.A: Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
options.B: Serum immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, IgM)
options.C: Liver enzymes (ALT and AST)
options.D: Fasting serum cholesterol and lipids

explanation: Immunoglobulins (antibodies) handle our humoral immunity. Checking IgG, IgA, and IgM levels helps us see if an antibody shortage is leaving the patient wide open to infections.

question: What is Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) mainly used for in post-abortion care?

options.A: Safely emptying the uterus of retained products of conception
options.B: Inducing long-term hormonal contraception to prevent pregnancy
options.C: Suturing cervical lacerations caused by traumatic instrumentation
options.D: Delivering strong intravenous antibiotics to treat pelvic sepsis

explanation: Exactly! MVA uses a safe, specialized syringe system to quickly clear out the uterine cavity during early pregnancy complications.

question: What is the main goal of the Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT)?

options.A: To calculate the correct medication dosage for the child
options.B: To perform a rapid, hands-off visual evaluation from the doorway
options.C: To measure the exact blood pressure and temperature
options.D: To listen carefully to heart murmurs with a stethoscope

explanation: You don't even need to touch the child right away! The PAT is a quick, visual tool you can use from the doorway to size up how sick a little one is.

question: In community health nursing, what do we mean by the word 'aggregate'?

options.A: All patients currently admitted to a tertiary hospital ward
options.B: The total number of healthcare staff working in a clinic
options.C: A specific subgroup of people sharing common characteristics
options.D: A collection of medical equipment used for immunizations

explanation: Great job! An aggregate is simply a group of people who share similar traits or health risks—like pregnant teenagers or market women—who we can care for together.

question: Which action best supports the emotional needs of a patient newly diagnosed with a blood disorder?

options.A: Leaving educational brochures on the bedside table and leaving
options.B: Providing active listening and validating their concerns
options.C: Directing all emotional questions strictly to the attending physician
options.D: Telling them not to worry because things could be worse

explanation: A new diagnosis is scary. Listening with empathy and validating their feelings builds trust and helps them cope better.

question: A patient has severe swelling around both eyes from a facial injury, making it impossible for them to open their eyes. How should you document the eye score?

options.A: Force the eyelids open to check for a spontaneous score
options.B: Record a score of 4 because they might open them later
options.C: Record a score of 2 because swelling counts as pain
options.D: Note eye opening as untestable due to swelling

explanation: Never force swollen eyelids open! Always document that the eye score is untestable due to local trauma or edema, keeping your patient safe and comfortable.

question: What happens inside the body to cause lymphoma?

options.A: Lymph vessels become blocked and burst
options.B: Abnormal lymphocytes multiply out of control and form tumors
options.C: The spleen stops filtering old cells
options.D: Bone marrow permanently stops making white cells

explanation: Lymphoma happens when those protective white blood cells (lymphocytes) go wild, dividing without stopping and building up in the lymph nodes.

question: Why is getting an accurate patient weight so important in clinical practice?

options.A: It measures total blood volume
options.B: It is used to calculate safe drug dosages
options.C: It determines the hospital billing category
options.D: It replaces the need for blood pressure checks

explanation: Exactly! Many powerful drugs—especially in children and critical care—are dosed strictly by weight in kilograms to keep the patient safe.

question: Why must a client eat a diet rich in carbohydrates for three days before a GTT?

options.A: To make sure the stomach is completely full before drinking the sweet syrup
options.B: To prevent false-positive results caused by low carbohydrate intake
options.C: To test how fast the liver can store extra glycogen reserves
options.D: To ensure the patient has plenty of energy to sit still during the test

explanation: If a patient restricts carbs beforehand, their body stops producing enough insulin, causing a fake diabetic spike during the test. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h3)

question: Which method is commonly used by nurse managers to evaluate if nursing documentation standards are being met?

options.A: Pharmacy stock counts
options.B: Patient dietary reviews
options.C: Chart audits
options.D: Staff fashion shows

explanation: Reviewing patient clinical records allows managers to see if charting and care standards are being followed accurately. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h7)

question: How did 20th-century pharmacology fundamentally differ from ancient healing practices?

options.A: It shifted from using crude natural mixtures to laboratory synthesis and targeted chemicals.
options.B: It abandoned all plant-based treatments in favor of spiritual healing.
options.C: It stopped testing medications on living tissues before human use.
options.D: It relied exclusively on oral traditions rather than written science.

explanation: Twentieth-century science moved past trial-and-error plant use to design and synthesize targeted chemical compounds in laboratories. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h5)

question: When packing a deep wound in a patient's home, what is the golden rule for placing the gauze inside?

options.A: Pack the wound tightly until it is completely firm to stop all bleeding.
options.B: Pack the wound loosely so it fills the space without putting pressure on the tissue.
options.C: Pack the wound using dry cotton balls for maximum absorption.
options.D: Pack only the top layer of skin and leave the deeper cavity empty.

explanation: Remember: never pack too tightly! Packing a wound too firmly cuts off the blood supply those new cells need to heal.

question: Which type of cervical traction involves putting metal pins directly into the skull bone?

options.A: Manual traction
options.B: Halter traction
options.C: Skin traction
options.D: Halo traction

explanation: Great job! Skeletal traction (like a halo device) uses metal pins right in the bone so it can handle much stronger pulling forces.

question: A patient in a rural community gets taeniasis after eating locally prepared meat. What was the most likely cause?

options.A: Eating undercooked pork or beef containing live larval cysts
options.B: Drinking unboiled stream water contaminated with tapeworm segments
options.C: Sharing eating utensils with an infected family member
options.D: Working barefoot in muddy soil containing free-living larvae

explanation: Correct! You catch intestinal taeniasis strictly by eating raw or undercooked meat that has live cysts in it. Always ensure your meat is well cooked!

question: Which agency is responsible for regulating food and drugs in Nigeria?

options.A: NAFDAC
options.B: Standard Organisation of Nigeria
options.C: National Youth Service Corps
options.D: Federal Ministry of Education

explanation: You've got this! NAFDAC is our watchdog, keeping watch over how drugs are made, imported, and sold across Nigeria.

question: Which hormones are mainly responsible for breaking down fat and muscle during the stress of surgery?

options.A: Cortisol and glucagon
options.B: Antidiuretic hormone
options.C: Insulin and estrogen
options.D: Thyroid stimulating hormone

explanation: Well done! Stress hormones like cortisol and glucagon shoot up during surgery to quickly mobilize energy for the body.

question: Why is checking the patient's blood creatinine level so important before an IVP?

options.A: To measure the concentration of red blood cells circulating in the plasma
options.B: To check if the patient has an active bacterial urinary infection
options.C: To calculate the exact amount of oral pain medication the patient needs
options.D: To ensure the kidneys can safely filter out the injected contrast dye

explanation: Creatinine tells us how well the kidneys are working. If they are struggling, the dye could make things worse, so we always check first!

question: A nurse is getting ready to give activated charcoal to a patient who swallowed poison. Which of these actions is a dangerous mistake?

options.A: Administering the charcoal through an intravenous infusion line
options.B: Confirming the time of the poison ingestion with family
options.C: Ensuring a suction machine is ready at the bedside
options.D: Checking the patient's airway before giving the liquid

explanation: Yikes! Activated charcoal belongs strictly in the stomach via the mouth or tube. Giving it into a vein (IV) is fatal. Always double-check your routes!

question: What is a direct positive outcome of strong teamwork in a hospital?

options.A: Higher rates of staff quitting their nursing jobs
options.B: Increased number of patients admitted without beds
options.C: Longer waiting times in the emergency department
options.D: Reduced medication errors and lower patient mortality

explanation: Spot on! When healthcare workers communicate and support each other well, mistakes drop and patients recover much faster.

question: Why do we use an intersectoral team approach in health care?

options.A: To combine different sectors to address the root causes of poor health
options.B: To train doctors to perform duties traditionally handled by agricultural workers
options.C: To increase the cost of running primary health care centers
options.D: To merge all community clinics into a single administrative unit

explanation: Great job! Health isn't just about medicine—it depends on social, economic, and environmental factors. Bringing different fields together helps us tackle these big issues at their core.

question: What protective layer forms around the egg cell during early follicular development?

options.A: Zona pellucida
options.B: Antrum membrane
options.C: Tunica albuginea
options.D: Corpus luteum

explanation: Spot on! The zona pellucida acts like a special protective coat around the egg and later helps sperm bind to it during fertilization.

question: Why does a pregnant woman's body absorb nutrients much better?

options.A: To slow down the overall digestion process in the stomach
options.B: To support the higher metabolic demands of the mother and fetus
options.C: To decrease the total amount of food the mother needs to consume
options.D: To prevent the mother from gaining any excess body weight

explanation: Great thinking! Her body works smarter to feed both her own tissues and the baby without running completely out of nutrients.

question: Why should a nurse look at laboratory results together with the physical exam instead of looking at labs alone?

options.A: Laboratory values are often incorrect and need physical confirmation.
options.B: Physical assessments can change laboratory values within minutes.
options.C: Hospital regulations forbid doctors from looking at labs without a nurse present.
options.D: Labs only provide part of the clinical picture and require patient context to be meaningful.

explanation: You nailed it! Numbers on a lab report don't tell the whole story. You always pair them with how the patient actually looks and feels.

question: Which induration measurement is considered positive for a patient with no known risk factors for tuberculosis?

options.A: 15 millimeters or more
options.B: 5 millimeters or more
options.C: 10 millimeters or more
options.D: 20 millimeters or more

explanation: For healthy individuals with no known exposure risks, the cut-off threshold for a positive test is 15 millimeters or greater. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h6)

question: Why is it helpful to ask a patient to empty their bladder before an exam?

options.A: It ensures the patient can stand up without assistance
options.B: It completely prevents any risk of a urinary tract infection
options.C: It lowers the patient's blood pressure significantly
options.D: It makes abdominal palpation more comfortable and accurate

explanation: A full bladder can cause discomfort and make it difficult for the nurse to feel deep abdominal organs properly. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h2)

question: A patient is prescribed an ipratropium inhaler. Which condition is this medication most likely treating?

options.A: Acute bacterial pneumonia
options.B: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
options.C: Severe hypertension
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Ipratropium is a bronchodilator commonly delivered by inhalation to open airways in respiratory conditions like COPD. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T6#GNS223_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which classroom setup helps prevent you from feeling sleepy during long lectures?

options.A: Bright neon paint and loud music
options.B: Proper lighting and good ventilation
options.C: Complete darkness with shut windows
options.D: Tight, cramped seating to save space

explanation: Fresh air and good lighting keep headaches and sleepiness away, helping you stay sharp and focused while your lecturer is talking.

question: Which fasting blood sugar level is usually the cutoff for diagnosing diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Less than 70 mg/dL
options.B: 100 to 110 mg/dL
options.C: 80 to 90 mg/dL
options.D: 126 mg/dL or higher

explanation: Keep this number handy for your clinical postings: 126 mg/dL or higher on two separate tests points toward a diabetes diagnosis.

question: What is the medical term for uncoordinated, clumsy muscle movements caused by a problem in the cerebellum?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Anosognosia
options.C: Ataxia
options.D: Aphasia

explanation: Ataxia simply means a lack of smooth muscle coordination, resulting in those jerky, unsteady movements we see in cerebellar issues. You're learning core clinical terms like a pro!

question: What is the job of the air inlet on a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: It locks the cork lid tightly into the ceramic jar
options.B: It lets the nurse pour medicine in while treating
options.C: It acts as a drain for extra water collection
options.D: It allows fresh air to mix with the rising steam

explanation: Exactly! The air inlet lets a bit of cooler room air mix with the vapor. This keeps the steam from being too scorching hot for the patient's mouth and throat.

question: What is a common mental health effect on a woman who faces constant pressure to bear a son?

options.A: Complete memory loss regarding her previous pregnancies
options.B: Sudden increase in physical stamina and pain tolerance
options.C: Chronic stress, anxiety, and clinical depression
options.D: Enhanced resilience and permanent emotional detachment

explanation: Constant fear of rejection, abuse, or failing family expectations takes a heavy toll on a mother's mental health.

question: Which side effect is very typical for ACE inhibitors like lisinopril?

options.A: Severe swelling of the lower legs
options.B: A persistent, dry, hacking cough
options.C: Excessive loss of potassium in urine
options.D: A dangerously fast resting heart rate

explanation: Spot on! ACE inhibitors can cause a buildup of a chemical called bradykinin in the lungs, leading to that classic annoying dry cough.

question: Why must a nurse instruct a patient to remove all metal jewelry and hairpins before a musculoskeletal CT scan?

options.A: The scanner's suction will pull metal objects into the machine.
options.B: Metal interacts with the magnetic field to cause severe burns.
options.C: Metal objects cause artifacts that ruin the clarity of the images.
options.D: Metal pieces block the patient from breathing properly.

explanation: Dense metal creates bright streaks and shadowing on CT scans, known as artifacts, which can hide important details about bones and joints. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h3)

question: What does the handy acronym AFASS help healthcare workers figure out about infant feeding?

options.A: The nutritional content of expressed breast milk
options.B: The rate of viral clearance in a nursing mother
options.C: The exact dosage of infant antiretroviral medications
options.D: The safety and suitability of replacement formula feeding

explanation: AFASS is a great tool! It checks if formula feeding is Affordable, Feasible, Acceptable, Sustainable, and Safe for the family's real-life situation.

question: What happens inside cells when they go without oxygen for too long (prolonged ischemia)?

options.A: They stop producing waste products entirely to save energy.
options.B: They begin storing large amounts of extra oxygen for later use.
options.C: They switch to anaerobic metabolism and produce excess lactic acid.
options.D: They rapidly multiply to replace the damaged surrounding tissue.

explanation: Without oxygen, cells panic a bit and switch to backup mode (anaerobic metabolism). This backup creates extra lactic acid, which causes that familiar ache.

question: What is the main rule for deciding what counts toward a country's Gross National Product (GNP)?

options.A: Approval by the World Health Organization
options.B: Physical location inside the national borders
options.C: Tax exemption status of the business
options.D: Citizenship or ownership by permanent residents

explanation: While GDP looks at geography, GNP focuses on who owns the production or who performs the work based on citizenship.

question: How is a painful muscle abscess caused by an unsterile injection usually managed?

options.A: Apply tight bandages to squeeze the trapped fluid out through the skin
options.B: Massage the lump firmly to help disperse the pus into surrounding tissue
options.C: Assist with surgical incision and drainage while maintaining sterile dressings
options.D: Advise the patient to ignore the lump until it dissolves on its own

explanation: Trapped pus has to come out! An abscess requires sterile incision and drainage, followed by proper wound care and antibiotics to help the patient heal.

question: Which nervous system kicks in when a patient practices slow, deep breathing?

options.A: Central nervous system
options.B: Somatic nervous system
options.C: Parasympathetic nervous system
options.D: Sympathetic nervous system

explanation: Deep breathing signals your vagus nerve to turn on the parasympathetic system—your body's wonderful 'rest-and-digest' mode that cools everything down.

question: Why does a target cell undergo upregulation when hormone levels remain low for a long time?

options.A: To prepare the cell to stop functioning completely
options.B: To turn off the gene expression of the cell
options.C: To increase its sensitivity to the scarce hormone
options.D: To destroy excess hormone molecules in the blood

explanation: Adding more receptors helps the cell catch and respond to whatever small amount of hormone is available. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h5)

question: During an exam, why do clinicians sometimes add potassium hydroxide (KOH) to a vaginal discharge sample?

options.A: To release a fishy odor in bacterial vaginosis
options.B: To lower the sample pH to an acidic level
options.C: To freeze the sample for laboratory transport
options.D: To stain the lactobacilli bacteria bright blue

explanation: It's called the 'whiff test'! Potassium hydroxide helps release those hidden smelly amines, making a fishy odor much easier to spot if BV is present. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h5)

question: Why shouldn't a patient start long-term uric acid-lowering drugs right in the middle of a severe gout attack?

options.A: It can cause sudden shifts in uric acid levels that worsen or prolong the acute inflammation
options.B: The medications are completely inactive while the joint is red and swollen
options.C: It permanently destroys the effectiveness of the drug for future use
options.D: It causes immediate kidney failure if taken during joint pain

explanation: Starting these meds mid-attack can cause uric acid levels to swing abruptly, making the existing flare last even longer.

question: What does the term Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) actually measure?

options.A: The percentage of water reabsorbed in the loop of Henle
options.B: The speed at which blood travels through the renal artery
options.C: The total amount of urine excreted per day
options.D: The volume of fluid filtered by the kidneys per minute

explanation: GFR quantifies how much filtrate the kidneys produce across all glomeruli in a given minute, serving as a key indicator of kidney health. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h5)

question: Which management theory assumes that employees dislike work and must be tightly controlled?

options.A: Systems theory
options.B: Theory Y
options.C: Theory X
options.D: Virtue ethics

explanation: Theory X is the pessimistic view of workers—it assumes people are lazy, want to avoid responsibility, and need a strict boss watching their every move.

question: What is the most important ingredient for any healthcare team to work well together?

options.A: Strict orders given only by physicians
options.B: Independent work without sharing notes
options.C: Focusing solely on hospital procedures
options.D: Mutual respect among all team members

explanation: Great thinking! Teamwork only works when everyone values what each person brings to the table.

question: What is the single most common trigger for Acute Glomerulonephritis globally and in Nigeria?

options.A: Streptococcal infection
options.B: Direct kidney trauma
options.C: A severe snake bite
options.D: High dietary salt intake

explanation: Post-streptococcal infection is overwhelmingly the most frequent cause of this type of nephritis. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary function of the human skin as a body system?

options.A: Regulating core body temperature through voluntary muscle contraction
options.B: Synthesizing primary digestive enzymes for nutrient breakdown
options.C: Acting as a protective barrier against external pathogens
options.D: Producing red blood cells for systemic circulation

explanation: The skin protects underlying structures from environmental threats, injury, and fluid loss. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T6#GNS213_U5_T6_h1)

question: As a student nurse or midwife, what is a key way you can promote safe motherhood in your community?

options.A: Educating families on danger signs and encouraging hospital delivery
options.B: Paying the hospital transport bills for poor pregnant women personally
options.C: Performing major surgeries inside primary health centers without doctors
options.D: Making laws to punish traditional birth attendants who work in villages

explanation: Community health education saves lives! Teaching families what warning signs to look out for helps them get moms to the hospital before it's too late.

question: Which of the following does NOT happen during untreated status epilepticus?

options.A: Extremely high body temperature from muscle activity
options.B: Dangerous buildup of acid in the body fluids
options.C: Severe oxygen shortage and brain tissue damage
options.D: Permanent drop in resting heart rate and low blood pressure

explanation: Correct! Instead of dropping, the heart rate and blood pressure actually shoot up due to extreme stress on the body. You're learning fast!

question: What is the main job of the ureters in our body?

options.A: Filter waste products out of the blood
options.B: Concentrate electrolytes in the renal pelvis
options.C: Store urine until it is ready for excretion
options.D: Transport urine from the kidneys to the bladder

explanation: You've got this! Think of the ureters as plumbing pipes that carry urine from the kidneys down into the bladder.

question: How does showing respect for a family's household customs help your patient care?

options.A: It allows the nurse to change household rules permanently
options.B: It reduces the financial cost of medical supplies
options.C: It builds trust and encourages the family to cooperate with the care plan
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never experience complications

explanation: Brilliant! When people feel respected in their own homes, they trust you more—and a trusting patient is much more likely to follow your health advice.

question: A young couple visits the clinic and mentions that multiple relatives on both sides died young from the same rare heart condition. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Prescribe blood pressure medication for both partners
options.B: Construct a pedigree chart and refer them for genetic assessment
options.C: Advise them to change their cooking oil immediately
options.D: Tell them not to worry because heart disease is completely normal

explanation: A pattern of early-onset disease in multiple relatives is a major red flag requiring formal genetic risk evaluation. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h3)

question: Why does wearing the correct glove size matter so much in clinical work?

options.A: It prevents tearing and keeps your fingers nimble
