options.D: Postnatal sepsis or infection

explanation: Bad-smelling lochia combined with a fever is a classic red flag for a uterine infection. You'll want to escalate this quickly for medical treatment!

question: How often should a bedbound patient usually be turned to prevent bedsores?

options.A: Every thirty minutes
options.B: Every two hours
options.C: Once every shift
options.D: Only when they complain of pain

explanation: Turning a patient at least every two hours takes pressure off bony areas and protects their skin from breaking down. Great routine to master for clinicals!

question: When should discharge planning ideally begin in a rehabilitation hospital?

options.A: Only after the final therapy session is completed
options.B: Twenty-four hours before the patient leaves
options.C: When the insurance company stops paying for care
options.D: The moment the patient is admitted to the facility

explanation: Spot on! Starting discharge planning early ensures that home equipment, family training, and support services are ready without a last-minute rush.

question: What is the primary focus of a hospice home facility?

options.A: Delivering intensive acute surgical care
options.B: Testing experimental medical treatments
options.C: Providing comfort and quality of life
options.D: Achieving a full recovery from terminal illness

explanation: Hospice care shifts away from curative treatments and focuses entirely on keeping the patient comfortable and improving their quality of life. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h1)

question: When body cells are completely cut off from oxygen, what backup energy system do they switch to?

options.A: Oxidative phosphorylation
options.B: Anaerobic metabolism
options.C: Glycolytic synthesis
options.D: Aerobic metabolism

explanation: When oxygen runs out, cells go into survival mode and use anaerobic metabolism. It keeps things going briefly, but makes lactic acid and less energy.

question: What is the crucial next step a patient must take right after using an emergency epinephrine auto-injector?

options.A: Lie flat on the floor with their feet elevated for two hours
options.B: Call their primary clinic doctor to schedule a routine follow-up
options.C: Go to the nearest hospital emergency room for evaluation
options.D: Take a strong oral antihistamine pill to prevent rebound

explanation: Spot on! Always head to the hospital. A secondary (biphasic) reaction can pop up hours later, and medical observation keeps the patient safe.

question: Which scenario best shows a functioning financial safety net for someone with a physical disability?

options.A: Depending entirely on street begging
options.B: Selling household properties for emergency surgery
options.C: Borrowing from high-interest money lenders monthly
options.D: Receiving regular disability grants and healthcare subsidies from the state

explanation: A true safety net catches people so they don't fall into extreme poverty when health crises hit.

question: Why is it important to ask if a patient has ever had surgery on their neck?

options.A: It can damage the thyroid or parathyroid glands
options.B: It stops the pancreas from producing insulin
options.C: It leads to chronic respiratory infections
options.D: It always causes permanent high blood pressure

explanation: Spot on! Because the thyroid and parathyroid glands live right in the neck, past surgeries there can sometimes accidentally disrupt hormone control.

question: What is the most serious risk when a patient takes anti-bleeding medications?

options.A: Severe low blood sugar
options.B: Excessive weight gain
options.C: Chronic hair loss
options.D: Unwanted blood clots traveling in the vessels

explanation: Because these drugs push the body to clot, overdoing it can cause clots to form and travel where they shouldn't, leading to serious trouble.

question: When writing a good research question, which of these is an absolute must?

options.A: It must guarantee positive results for the hospital
options.B: It must be broad enough to change every nursing policy at once
options.C: It must use complex Latin terms to sound professional
options.D: It must be feasible to answer with available time and resources

explanation: Keep it realistic! Feasible simply means you have the time, money, and access to patients to actually finish the study without stressing out.

question: When MUST you wear disposable gloves during morning hygiene care?

options.A: During every single task from start to finish
options.B: When touching body fluids or broken skin
options.C: Only when brushing the patient's teeth
options.D: Every time you walk into the room

explanation: Brilliant! Gloves are shields against germs found in blood, urine, stool, spit, and cuts on the skin.

question: How does a lethargic patient usually act during an assessment?

options.A: Completely unresponsive even to painful stimuli
options.B: Fully awake and answers every question instantly
options.C: Aggressive and physically combative with staff
options.D: Drowsy and drifts off to sleep when not stimulated

explanation: A lethargic patient wakes up when you talk to them or touch them, but they tend to drift right back off to sleep the moment you stop interacting.

question: Why is the time right after breakfast often the best time to try having a bowel movement?

options.A: Stomach acid levels are at their lowest point of the day
options.B: Blood pressure peaks and helps push waste forward
options.C: Eating food triggers a natural wave of activity in the colon
options.D: Digestive enzymes are most active in the rectum then

explanation: Eating stimulates the gastrocolic reflex, which increases muscle contractions in the colon and creates a natural urge to go. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is a major advantage of eating seasonal local fruits here in Nigeria?

options.A: They contain no natural carbohydrates at all
options.B: They last indefinitely without refrigeration
options.C: They are imported directly from foreign countries
options.D: They are more affordable and readily available

explanation: Exactly! Buying local and in-season means fresher fruits that are kind to your wallet and easy to find in our markets.

question: What is the main goal of ergonomics in the workplace?

options.A: Inspecting the concrete strength of the building
options.B: Setting exact employee salaries and bonuses
options.C: Fitting workstations and tools to match human body limits
options.D: Managing the menu in the staff cafeteria

explanation: Exactly! Ergonomics is all about designing work tools and chairs to fit the human body, preventing physical strain.

question: A patient with unsteady balance and dizziness is admitted to the medical ward. What is the most immediate safety risk to prevent?

options.A: A wrong-site surgical procedure
options.B: A severe hospital-acquired infection
options.C: A physical fall leading to injury
options.D: An accidental medication overdose

explanation: Unsteadiness and dizziness directly increase the likelihood of slips and falls, making fall precautions the priority intervention for this patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h3)

question: What is the main thing sedative medications do to the body?

options.A: Increased skeletal muscle contraction
options.B: Central nervous system depression
options.C: Enhanced sensory perception
options.D: Central nervous system stimulation

explanation: Sedatives help you relax by slowing down brain activity and calming the central nervous system. Think of it like hitting the slow-down button in your brain! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h1)

question: Which bedside check gives immediate confirmation that an endotracheal tube is correctly placed in the trachea?

options.A: Daily routine chest radiography results
options.B: End-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO2) monitoring
options.C: Measurement of peak inspiratory pressure
options.D: Arterial blood gas analysis drawn after 30 minutes

explanation: ETCO2 detectors quickly show exhaled carbon dioxide right at the bedside, proving the tube went down the windpipe and not the stomach.

question: Which symptom should the nurse instruct the patient to report immediately after arthrocentesis?

options.A: Feeling thirsty after the test
options.B: Fever and worsening joint pain
options.C: Mild itching around the bandage
options.D: Slight drowsiness from resting

explanation: Fever and increasing pain are key warning signs of a developing joint infection after the procedure. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h7)

question: A patient says, 'My cough is gone after a month, so I want to stop my TB pills.' What is your best response as a nurse?

options.A: Take only the rifampicin and throw away the other pills since they cause too many side effects
options.B: Stop the drugs immediately since the absence of a cough proves the lungs are fully healed
options.C: Switch to half the dose for the remaining months to save money on prescription refills
options.D: Continue taking all pills for the full months prescribed to kill hidden germs and prevent resistance

explanation: Feeling better doesn't mean the germs are gone! Patients must finish their full course to wipe out hidden bacteria and avoid resistance.

question: Which ethical theory focuses strictly on creating the greatest good for the greatest number of people?

options.A: Classical control
options.B: Virtue ethics
options.C: Utilitarianism
options.D: Deontology

explanation: Think of utilitarianism as the 'greater good' approach. It weighs decisions based on which option brings the most overall benefit to the biggest group.

question: A patient with a broken hip is placed in skin traction mainly for which reason?

options.A: Preventing deep vein thrombosis in the affected leg
options.B: Immediate rehabilitation and walking exercise practice
options.C: Permanent alignment so surgical repair is no longer required
options.D: Temporary stabilization and comfort while waiting for surgery

explanation: Think of skin traction here as a helpful temporary pause—it keeps the leg steady and comfortable until the surgical team is ready. You're doing great!

question: As a nurse, what is one of your most important duties right before the patient goes for surgery?

options.A: Verifying that the informed consent form is signed
options.B: Teaching the patient how to change their wound dressing
options.C: Ordering a special post-operative hospital diet
options.D: Scheduling the patient's follow-up clinic appointment

explanation: Great job! Making sure the consent form is signed proves the patient understands the surgery, its risks, and has agreed to it before heading to the theater.

question: Why does lacking thiamine cause brain cells to die so quickly?

options.A: It disrupts critical energy pathways and glucose metabolism in neurons
options.B: It causes massive bacterial infections inside the cerebrospinal fluid
options.C: It triggers an autoimmune attack directly targeting the myelin sheath
options.D: It increases intracranial pressure by blocking the reabsorption of CSF

explanation: Think of thiamine as the spark plug for brain cells to burn glucose. Without it, the cells literally starve for energy and shut down.

question: On a lab report, what does a "shift to the left" in white blood cells usually tell the healthcare team?

options.A: An allergic reaction rather than a bacterial infection
options.B: A recovery phase where all blood counts return to normal
options.C: An increased release of immature white blood cells
options.D: A complete failure of the bone marrow to produce cells

explanation: You nailed it! When a severe infection drains the mature white blood cells, the bone marrow starts rushing out baby cells ('bands') early to help out.

question: What is the anatomical term for the neck region?

options.A: Thoracic
options.B: Cephalic
options.C: Cervical
options.D: Lumbar

explanation: The neck is anatomically referred to as the cervical region, linking the head to the chest. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h2)

question: What makes thyroid hormones act a bit differently than other amino acid-derived hormones?

options.A: They are large proteins made of hundreds of linked amino acids
options.B: They only function within the nervous system as fast neurotransmitters
options.C: They cannot travel in the bloodstream without dissolving in red blood cells
options.D: They are fat-soluble and enter cells to bind intracellular receptors

explanation: Even though they start from an amino acid, thyroid hormones behave like fat-loving steroids—they slip right inside the cell to do their work. Tricky, but you'll never forget it now!

question: A massive movement of young people from rural farming villages into a crowded capital city is an example of which demographic process?

options.A: High fertility
options.B: Child mortality
options.C: Population capping
options.D: Internal migration

explanation: When people move from one place to another within the same country—like leaving the village for the city—we call it internal migration.

question: What is the main job of active vitamin D once processed by the kidneys?

options.A: To lower blood pressure by widening blood vessels
options.B: To speed up the filtration rate of the glomerulus
options.C: To stimulate red blood cell production in marrow
options.D: To promote calcium and phosphorus absorption in the gut

explanation: Spot on! Active vitamin D helps your intestines absorb calcium and phosphorus from your food so your body has what it needs for strong bones.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to using living wills in clinical practice?

options.A: Vaguely written instructions like 'no heroic measures'
options.B: Having too many copies of the document easily available to doctors
options.C: Family members disputing the wishes during an emergency
options.D: Documents being left at home instead of brought to the hospital

explanation: Having too many accessible copies is rarely a problem; the usual issue is that documents are hidden at home or poorly written. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h6)

question: Why is it crucial to keep track of a patient's total daily dose of paracetamol (acetaminophen)?

options.A: It causes rapid kidney failure within an hour
options.B: Too much of it can cause severe liver damage
options.C: Overdosing immediately stops breathing
options.D: Higher doses cause heavy stomach bleeding

explanation: Spot on! The liver breaks down paracetamol. If the daily limit is crossed, toxic byproducts build up and can cause serious liver injury.

question: Which question type is best for encouraging a patient to tell their story in their own words?

options.A: Closed-ended questions
options.B: Multiple-choice questions
options.C: Leading questions
options.D: Open-ended questions

explanation: Open-ended questions allow patients to elaborate freely without limiting their responses to a single word. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the primary clinical difference between acute pain and chronic pain?

options.A: Acute pain only affects internal organs, while chronic pain is restricted to skin and muscles
options.B: Chronic pain responds immediately to simple opioids, whereas acute pain requires complex nerve blocks
options.C: Acute pain serves as a sudden warning sign of tissue injury, while chronic pain persists long after healing
options.D: Acute pain causes severe anxiety, while chronic pain never has any psychological impact

explanation: Acute pain acts as a protective alarm for recent injury, whereas chronic pain lasts past normal healing time and becomes a long-term condition. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a direct complication of prolonged bed rest?

options.A: Development of atelectasis
options.B: Enhanced muscle endurance
options.C: Blood clot formation
options.D: Pressure injury formation

explanation: Bed rest weakens muscles rather than building endurance! The other three options are classic risks we try hard to prevent in immobilized patients.

question: How do parks and tree-lined streets help clean up city air?

options.A: They increase the temperature of the city to destroy bacteria
options.B: They absorb carbon dioxide and trap dust particles
options.C: They produce chemical gases that neutralize industrial smoke
options.D: They block all wind currents so microbes cannot travel

explanation: You nailed it! Plants act like natural filters, taking in carbon dioxide and catching dust right on their leaves.

question: Why is it dangerous for a nurse to show judgment or anger toward a patient with abortion complications?

options.A: It legally terminates the nurse's professional employment contract
options.B: It discourages the patient from speaking honestly about what substances were used
options.C: It permanently cures the underlying infection causing the sepsis
options.D: It forces the hospital to close down its emergency department

explanation: Spot on! When patients are afraid of being judged, they hide vital secrets, making it much harder for you to save their lives.

question: What is the main purpose of formative evaluation?

options.A: To give ongoing feedback to help you learn better
options.B: To check the school's financial budget
options.C: To pass the national licensing exam
options.D: To decide your final GPA for graduation

explanation: Formative evaluation is your friendly guide while you are still learning—it gives you feedback so you can improve before any big stakes exam.

question: Why do traditional chemotherapy drugs commonly cause side effects like hair loss and mucosal sores?

options.A: They cause the patient's immune system to attack hair follicles
options.B: They attack all rapidly dividing cells, both cancerous and normal
options.C: They block the formation of protective fibrous tumor capsules
options.D: They stimulate normal cells to enter permanent resting phases

explanation: Traditional chemotherapy targets rapidly dividing cells, which inadvertently damages healthy tissues with high turnover like hair follicles and gut linings. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h8)

question: What physical property helps a drug cross a mucous membrane in a hurry?

options.A: Large molecular weight
options.B: High lipid solubility
options.C: Inability to dissolve in water
options.D: Strong acidic composition

explanation: Like dissolves like! Because cell membranes are made of fats (lipids), fat-loving (lipid-soluble) drugs slip right through them with ease.

question: How does your brain figure out which direction a sound is coming from?

options.A: By measuring how much earwax blocks the external auditory canal
options.B: By tracking the movement of the stapes bone against the oval window
options.C: By comparing the slight time and loudness differences between both ears
options.D: By analyzing the chemical balance of perilymph fluid in the cochlea

explanation: Because your ears are on opposite sides of your head, a sound hits the closer ear a split second faster and louder than the other. Your brain calculates this tiny difference to pinpoint the direction!

question: Which of these is NOT a good topic for patient education regarding dietary supplements?

options.A: Bringing all supplement containers to clinic appointments for review
options.B: Checking for valid NAFDAC registration numbers on product labels
options.C: How to manufacture herbal capsules at home in your kitchen
options.D: Reporting unusual side effects or symptoms to a healthcare provider

explanation: As nurses, we teach safety, checking labels, and reporting side effects—we definitely don't encourage brewing or making DIY pills at home!

question: Which white blood cells are our most abundant and fast-acting fighters against bacteria?

options.A: Neutrophils
options.B: Basophils
options.C: Memory cells
options.D: Eosinophils

explanation: Well done! Neutrophils are usually the very first white blood cells to rush to the scene of a fresh bacterial infection.

question: Which brain structure acts as the ultimate master control center for the autonomic nervous system?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Occipital lobe

explanation: The hypothalamus is the boss! It coordinates all visceral signals to keep your internal environment (homeostasis) stable and balanced.

question: Why do we call the pituitary gland the 'master gland' of the body?

options.A: It directly controls the activity of several other hormone glands.
options.B: It makes every single hormone needed to keep you alive without help.
options.C: It controls your conscious thought and memory along with the brain.
options.D: It is simply the largest endocrine organ located inside the skull.

explanation: You got this! It earns the title 'master gland' because its hormones act like boss signals telling other glands—like your thyroid and adrenals—when to release their own hormones.

question: A patient sitting in a wheelchair for long hours is most likely to develop pressure sores on which specific area?

options.A: Ischial tuberosities
options.B: Occipital bone
options.C: Bridge of the nose
options.D: Anterior patella

explanation: The ischial tuberosities are simply your sitting bones! When a patient sits for too long, these bones take the heavy brunt of the body weight. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h2)

question: Which skin layer receives an intradermal injection?

options.A: Epidermis
options.B: Dermis
options.C: Subcutaneous tissue
options.D: Muscle layer

explanation: The needle is inserted into the middle layer of the skin, known as the dermis, which sits right beneath the outer epidermis. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h2)
